title: The Guidebook
subtitle: A field manual — replace this subtitle with one short, evocative line.
author: Author name

chapters.title: Layout reference
chapters.description: This first chapter is a showcase of every supported step layout. Use it to choose the right combination of image type and callouts for your guide.

steps.title: Single — plain
steps.instruction: One phone-shaped screen, centered, with the instruction beneath. Use this for the majority of mobile screenshots.

steps.title: Single — with callouts
steps.instruction: Same phone-shaped screen, with a column of callouts to the right pointing out elements on the screen.

callouts.title: Header
callouts.body: Describe the labelled area at the top of the screen.

callouts.title: Action
callouts.body: Explain the primary control the user interacts with here.

callouts.title: Required
callouts.body: Flag a precondition or required field before the user can continue.

steps.title: Double — plain
steps.instruction: Two phone screens side-by-side. Use for before/after, comparison of two options, or the result of an action on the previous screen.

steps.title: Double — with callouts
steps.instruction: Two screens side-by-side with a callouts column. Use when both screens need annotation but you don't want to imply a flow direction between them.

callouts.title: Left screen
callouts.body: Identify a key element on the first screen.

callouts.title: Right screen
callouts.body: Identify a key element on the second screen.

callouts.title: Compare
callouts.body: A softer side-remark on the difference between the two states.

steps.title: Double — arrow + callouts
steps.instruction: Two screens with an arrow tracking the user's path, plus callouts on the right pointing out specific elements.

callouts.title: Inventory
callouts.body: Inventory is auto-populated from your last session.

callouts.title: Quantity
callouts.body: Tap to increase or decrease the amount.

callouts.title: Required
callouts.body: Take a photo before tapping Continue, otherwise the form will not submit.

steps.title: Single-wide — plain
steps.instruction: One wide screen spanning the full double-layout width — use for landscape captures, tablet UI, or wider composite screens.

steps.title: Single-wide — with callouts
steps.instruction: Single-wide image with a callouts column to the right. The wide slot shrinks to make room for the callouts while keeping the same aspect ratio.

callouts.title: Toolbar
callouts.body: Identify the controls along the top of the wide layout.

callouts.title: Detail
callouts.body: A softer side-remark for less critical info.

steps.title: Single — callouts below
steps.instruction: Same single screen, but with callouts laid out below in a 2-column grid. Use when you have several short annotations and want to give the screen its full width on the page.

callouts.title: Header
callouts.body: The labelled area at the top of the screen.

callouts.title: Action
callouts.body: The primary control the user taps to continue.

callouts.title: Status
callouts.body: Persistent status indicator — usually visible across screens.

callouts.title: Empty state
callouts.body: Shown until the user has at least one saved item.

callouts.title: Required
callouts.body: Must be filled before the user can submit.

callouts.title: Footer
callouts.body: Secondary navigation lives at the bottom.

steps.title: Double — callouts below
steps.instruction: Two screens stacked side-by-side with an arrow, callouts below in a grid. Best when each numbered callout corresponds to a labelled spot across both screens.

callouts.title: Tap the menu
callouts.body: Opens the navigation drawer.

callouts.title: Pick a list
callouts.body: Choose any list to view its contents.

callouts.title: Sort order
callouts.body: Defaults to most-recent first.

callouts.title: Required
callouts.body: A list must contain at least one item before sharing.

steps.title: Single-wide — callouts below (3 cols)
steps.instruction: Wide layout with a 3-column grid of callouts beneath. Set `calloutCols: 3` for denser annotation when callout bodies are short.

callouts.title: Search
callouts.body: Searches across all open documents.

callouts.title: Filters
callouts.body: Stack filters to narrow results.

callouts.title: Sort
callouts.body: Sort by date, name or size.

callouts.title: Tip
callouts.body: Hold ⌥ to multi-select rows.

callouts.title: Tip
callouts.body: Double-click a header to auto-fit.

callouts.title: Heads up
callouts.body: Selection is cleared on filter change.

steps.title: Single — custom height
steps.instruction: Override `imageHeight` when a screenshot is longer than a standard phone screen (e.g. a scrolling capture). Width is unaffected; the slot just grows taller.

steps.title: Double — per-slot sizing
steps.instruction: Use `imageSizes` to set width and/or height for each slot independently — for example, a phone screen next to a slightly taller wider screenshot.

steps.title: Single — full-width callouts below
steps.instruction: Set `calloutCols: 1` to give each callout the full page width below the screen. Best when callout bodies are long sentences or paragraphs.

callouts.title: Why this screen matters
callouts.body: Walks the user through the most important decision they'll make in the whole flow. Give it the spotlight it deserves.

callouts.title: Tap the primary action
callouts.body: The CTA at the bottom advances to the next step. Notice that it stays disabled until every required field above it is filled in correctly.

callouts.title: Don't skip this
callouts.body: If the user backs out at this point, the partial entry is discarded — there is no draft saved on the device or server.

steps.title: Multi-row — stack layouts on one page
steps.instruction: Use an `images` array instead of a single `image`. Each entry is its own row — any mix of single, double or single-wide — stacked down the page. If the combined stack would overflow, every image scales down (aspect preserved) until it fits.

images.title: Row one — a wide hero
images.instruction: A single-wide screen leads the page.

images.title: Row two — a before / after pair
images.instruction: A double row sits beneath it, sharing the leftover vertical space.

steps.title: Multi-row — callouts per row
steps.instruction: Each row carries its own `callouts` and `calloutLayout`. Keep callout counts modest so the whole stack still fits the page.

callouts.title: Field
callouts.body: Annotate an element on the top screen.

callouts.title: Required
callouts.body: Flag the must-do action here.

callouts.title: Tap
callouts.body: Opens the next screen.

callouts.title: Result
callouts.body: Shows the updated state.

steps.title: Per-image border — framed vs. borderless
steps.instruction: Every image is framed with a 6px border by default. Set `border: false` to drop the frame — handy for screenshots that already include their own chrome or a full-bleed graphic.

chapters.title: Working through the process
chapters.description: The middle chapter. Use it to expand on the technique introduced in chapter one and to demonstrate variations.

steps.instruction: Begin with a brief re-orientation — remind the reader where they left off.
Introduce the core technique of this chapter. The pair of screens shows the tap and the resulting state.
Show a common variation, with the image highlighting the difference.
End with a checkpoint — the left screen is what the reader should see; the right is the next view they'll move into.

chapters.title: Finishing well
chapters.description: The closing chapter. Tie everything together and leave the reader with a clear sense of completion.

steps.instruction: Inspect the work. The two screens compare the expected and the actual result.
Make final adjustments — small changes only at this stage.
